The planet of voice is the strongest thing in his chart — and the most buried.

TL;DR

India's most famous voice, computed

Mercury runs speech, voice and script. In his birth chart it is exalted — the single strongest placement he has. It is also combust: sitting 25 arc-minutes from the Sun, close enough to be burned right off the sky.
Twenty-five arc-minutes is about the width of a full moon. That is how close the voice-planet is to being swallowed by the Sun in his chart — strongest and most hidden, the same placement, at the same moment.

The public record does the rest of the talking. He failed an All India Radio newsreader audition in the late 1960s. Roughly thirty years later, that same voice was the most recognisable sound in India. This page will not tell you the chart caused that. It will show you that the chart wrote the tension down, and let you decide what to do with it.

The rise, mapped

Fifty-seven years, two collapses

A rejected radio voice, a superstar, a near-fatal accident, a bankruptcy, and then the biggest second act Indian television has produced.

How to read this: the line is roughly his public standing, from a shipping-firm desk job in Kolkata to hosting his eighteenth season of a quiz show at 83. The band underneath is not a dasha chart — it is the birth-time problem, drawn to scale. Every other celebrity astrology page will show you a confident timeline here. We can't, and the band shows you exactly why.

That red line is the whole problem. His birth nakshatra decides which planet opens his Vimshottari dasha sequence — Chitra hands it to Mars, Swati hands it to Rahu. The two circulating birth times sit on opposite sides of it. So the eras below are dated from the public record, not from a dasha. We'd rather show you the gap than paper over it.

1942–1968 · THE POET'S SON

Almost named "Revolution"

Allahabad 11 October 1942
  • Born in Allahabad — now Prayagraj — to the Hindi poet Harivansh Rai Bachchan and Teji Bachchan. His parents planned to call him Inquilab, "revolution", after the slogan Inquilab Zindabad. The poet Sumitranandan Pant suggested Amitabh instead.
  • Boys' High School in Allahabad, then Sherwood College in Nainital, then a B.Sc. from Kirori Mal College in Delhi in 1962.
  • Before any of the films: a business-executive job at Bird & Company, a shipping firm in Kolkata. And an audition to read the news for All India Radio, which he did not pass.
🔭 What the sky had already fixed: Mercury exalted and combust, Venus debilitated, Jupiter exalted. None of it needs a birth time — those are the positions on 11 October 1942 at every hour of that day.

1969–1972 · THE QUIET YEARS

A voice-over, then a long run of films nobody watched

Bhuvan Shome → Anand 1969–1971
  • His first screen credit was not a face at all — it was his voice, narrating Mrinal Sen's Bhuvan Shome (1969). The instrument arrived before the actor did.
  • Acting debut the same year in Saat Hindustani. Then a stretch of films that largely came and went.
  • The exception: Anand (1971), opposite Rajesh Khanna, which won him a Filmfare award for Best Supporting Actor and told the industry something it hadn't noticed yet.
🔭 Mercury in Chitra, exalted, retrograde. Retrograde is traditionally read as a planet that works inward first and shows results late. Read that as texture, not as a cause — the delay is documented history either way.

The angry young man arrives, and doesn't leave for a decade

Zanjeer · Deewaar · Sholay 1973 · 1975 · 1975
  • Zanjeer (1973) is the hinge. A furious, near-silent police officer — the opposite of the singing romantic hero the industry was selling — and it worked.

🔭 Four planets in Virgo, inside 10 degrees. A stellium that tight concentrates enormous weight in one sign. Traditional reading: whatever that sign governs becomes the whole personality. It doesn't tell you when — nothing in his chart can, without the minute.

A year lost, and one term as an MP

Coolie 26 July 1982
  • On 26 July 1982, filming a fight scene for Coolie in Bangalore, he was involved in a near-fatal accident. He has spoken about it publicly many times since; the whole country kept vigil for weeks.

🔭 Nothing here is astrological, and that is deliberate. AxtroShastra does not tie events like this to anyone's chart, on any page. A chart is not a cause and it is not a warning. The date is on the record; the meaning is his to tell, and he has.

He built a studio. It took the house down with it.

ABCL founded 1996 · collapsed 1997
  • Amitabh Bachchan Corporation Ltd was founded in 1996 as a full-service entertainment company — films, events, distribution, music.
  • It collapsed financially and operationally in 1997. In April 1999 the Bombay High Court restrained him from selling his bungalow while loan-recovery proceedings brought by Canara Bank were pending.

🔭 Venus, debilitated. Venus governs money, luxury and being wanted; in Virgo it has no natural support. Traditional astrology reads a debilitated planet as one that gives late and only after real effort. Note what that does not say: it doesn't say bankruptcy, and it can't date one.

He fixed it with the exact thing that once got him rejected

Kaun Banega Crorepati since July 2000 · season 18 airing now
  • Kaun Banega Crorepati launched in July 2000. What it sold was not his face — it was a man talking to strangers, one question at a time. The voice, at last, doing the whole job by itself.

🔭 Mercury, again. The planet is exalted and it is burnt. A career that starts with a failed radio audition and ends up being carried by a microphone is the same tension, told twice.
Real talk

Two things people actually search for

One is a genuine astrological problem. One is money. Both are public record, and neither gets a fake answer here.

🕰️ The birth time nobody can agree on
What's public

Two versions circulate widely. Bachchan himself has said he was born between 3 and 4 in the morning; most Indian astrology sites use 3:30 a.m. His father's autobiography describes the birth as taking place in the early afternoon, and a large family of charts — including the reference chart in our own test suite — uses 4:00 p.m.

Astro-Databank rates his data DD: "dirty data", conflicting sources, no verified record. That rating is the honest one.

What the chart does with it

We ran his chart at ten-minute steps across the whole of 11 October 1942 and then narrowed to the second. The Moon leaves Chitra and enters Swati at 08:47 a.m.

3:30 a.m. is Chitra. 4:00 p.m. is Swati. Chitra's lord is Mars; Swati's is Rahu. Since the birth nakshatra is what sets the Vimshottari dasha order, the two times don't just shift dates — they produce two entirely different sequences.

A wrinkle almost nobody accounts for: India ran on Indian War Time, UTC+6:30, from September 1942 to October 1945. His birth day falls inside that window, so a clock time of 3:30 that morning is an hour further from GMT than the +5:30 nearly every site assumes. It doesn't change a single sign — it just adds one more reason not to trust the minute.

💸 The bankruptcy he talks about himself
What's public

ABCL's collapse in 1997 left him personally exposed. By April 1999 the Bombay High Court had restrained him from selling his Mumbai bungalow while Canara Bank's loan-recovery cases were pending. He has described the period in his own words in interviews and on his blog for two decades since — including going back to producers to ask for work at 57.

This is his own telling, not an allegation by anyone. No wrongdoing was alleged or found; a company failed.

What the chart notes

His Venus is debilitated — the money-and-comfort planet in the sign where classical texts give it the least support. That is a permanent feature of his chart, true on the day he was born and true on the day Sholay opened.

Which is precisely the point: a placement that never changes cannot explain an event that happened once. It describes a texture — earned late, rarely handed over. It does not date a bankruptcy, and we are not going to pretend it does.

Being straight with you: nothing above claims the chart caused anything. The life facts are public record; the astrology beside them is traditional interpretation offered for entertainment. On this page you will not find a house-level reading, a manglik verdict, a dated dasha, or any suggestion that a birth chart predicts or explains what happened to him. Those need a verified birth minute — and some of them simply aren't something we do.

  • His very first screen credit, in 1969, was a voice-over — not a role.
  • Thirty-one years later, a quiz show built almost entirely around him speaking to one nervous stranger at a time pulled him out of debt and made him a bigger household name than the films ever had.

🔭 The chart bit: Mercury exalted in its own sign, and combust. A planet at maximum dignity, standing too close to the Sun to be seen. If you were writing that as a story rather than a chart, you'd call it on the nose.

  • 1999: restrained by a court from selling his own house while a bank pursued recovery.
  • 2005, 2009 and 2015: National Film Awards for Best Actor for Black, Paa and Piku — the last of them at 72, in a film where he played a constipated Bengali retiree.

What the sky wrote

Seven placements. Seven receipts.

Every position below is computed for 11 October 1942, Allahabad — Swiss Ephemeris, Lahiri ayanamsa, our own engine. Every one of them is identical at 3:30 a.m. and at 4:00 p.m., which is the only reason they are on this page at all. The full nine-graha table is in Lesson 02.

Mercury · 24°17′ Virgo

The strongest planet in his chart is also the most buried

  • It is also combust: 0°25′ from the Sun. Combustion is what classical texts call a planet standing so close to the Sun that it's lost in the glare. Twenty-five arc-minutes is roughly the width of a full moon.

  • Chitra nakshatra, pada 1. Chitra's symbol is a bright single jewel; its name means "the brilliant one".

The glamour planet, in the sign that gives it nothing

  • Venus runs charm, money, comfort, beauty and being wanted. Virgo is its debilitation — the single sign where classical astrology gives Venus the least to work with.

Four planets in one sign, inside ten degrees

  • But it isn't alone. Sun, Mercury, Venus and Mars are all in Virgo, spanning 14°32′ to 24°17′ — under ten degrees of sky between the four of them. That is a genuinely tight stellium.

The rashi is certain. The star it sits in is not.

  • The Moon is the planet most Vedic "what's your rashi" answers actually mean. His sits in Libra (Tula) — and it does so at every single minute of 11 October 1942. That part is not in dispute at all.

  • Ketu, always exactly opposite, sits at 8°48′ Aquarius in Shatabhisha — the star of the healer and the hundred physicians.
  • Both nodes compute as retrograde, which is normal: by the standard calculation the lunar nodes are retrograde essentially all the time. It is not a special flag on his chart.
🔭 Rahu in Magha, the throne-room star. A man whose most-quoted early fact is whose son he is, with the lineage star holding his fame planet. Read it as poetry, not proof.

Actually learn this

Astrology, but make it make sense

Zero background needed. Read this once and you can decode the chart above yourself — no astrologer required.

LESSON 01

What a birth chart even is

It's a photograph of the sky taken from one spot on Earth at one moment — where every planet was sitting, frozen. A janam kundli is that snapshot, drawn as a grid.

Vedic astrology treats it as the raw material you were handed, not your fate. A starting kit, not a script.

His: 11 October 1942, Allahabad. That sky had Mercury exalted and burnt, Jupiter exalted, Venus debilitated, and four planets crowded into a single sign. Those four facts do most of the work on this page.
LESSON 02

The nine planets, and what each one does

Nine of them — the seven visible bodies plus the two lunar nodes. Think of them as nine departments, each running one part of life.

Degrees are for 3:30 a.m.; at 4:00 p.m. every one of these signs, dignities and nakshatras is the same except the Moon's, which is the row flagged ⚠. That is the entire practical difference between the two disputed times, and it is a big one — Lesson 05 explains why.

LESSON 03

Why "which sign" actually matters

Every planet has signs where it's comfortable and signs where it struggles. Same planet, different room.

  • Exalted — the planet's best possible sign. Full strength. His Mercury (Virgo) and Jupiter (Cancer).
  • Own sign — it owns the place. Mercury also owns Virgo, so it gets both at once.
  • Debilitated — the sign directly opposite its exaltation. Least support. His Venus (Virgo).
  • A stellium — several planets crowded into one sign. Not automatically good or bad, just a lot of weight in one room. His Virgo holds four.
His scorecard: two exalted (Mercury, Jupiter), one debilitated (Venus), four sharing Virgo (Sun, Mercury, Venus, Mars), the rest neutral. Two exalted planets is genuinely uncommon. Having one of them burnt by the Sun is what makes this chart interesting rather than just strong.
LESSON 04

Combustion — the bit almost nobody explains

When a planet passes very close to the Sun in the sky, you literally cannot see it — it's lost in the glare. Classical Jyotish calls that combust (asta), and treats it as a planet whose strength is present but obscured.

Each planet has its own orb. Mercury's is about 13°; Mars's about 17°; Venus's about 9°.

In his chart:
Mercury is 0°25′ from the Sun — deep inside the orb. About the width of a full moon.
Mars is 1°36′ away — also combust.
Venus is 9°20′ away — just outside its 9° orb, so it escapes. Debilitated, but not burnt.

So the sky on 11 October 1942 handed him the strongest possible Mercury and then stood it directly in front of a spotlight. Both things are true at once, and that's the honest reading — not "his voice was destined", not "his voice was cursed".
LESSON 05

Dashas — and why we will not print his

Planets don't all act at once. Vedic astrology has them take turns running your life, for years at a stretch, in a fixed order. A planet's turn is a dasha. This is where every celebrity astrology page gets its "he was in his Saturn period when X happened" line.

Here is the part those pages don't tell you: the whole ladder is generated from one input — the exact position of the Moon at birth, specifically which nakshatra it was in and how far through that nakshatra it had travelled.

What we computed, and why it stops us:
His Moon crosses from Chitra into Swati at 08:47 a.m. on 11 October 1942.

Chitra's lord is Mars. Swati's lord is Rahu.
The 3:30 a.m. version therefore opens his life with a Mars mahadasha. The 4:00 p.m. version opens it with a Rahu mahadasha — a different planet, running a different number of years, handing over to a different successor, and so on for all nine.

These are not two versions of the same timeline. They are two different timelines.

And even if you picked one, the dates would still be unusable: the Moon moves about 13° a day through nakshatras only 13°20′ wide, so the position within the star — which is what sets the starting balance — sweeps almost its entire range across a single day. We swept his in ten-minute steps: the end of the first mahadasha lands anywhere between 1942 and 1960 depending on the hour.

So there is no dasha table on this page. Not a hedged one, not an "approximate" one. If you find one elsewhere for him, the site picked a birth time and didn't mention it.
LESSON 06

How we found 08:47 — the actual method

Worth showing, because it's arithmetic rather than opinion, and you could check it yourself.

We computed his chart at ten-minute intervals across the entire day — 145 charts — and watched the Moon's nakshatra. Coarse steps are dangerous here: a three-hour sweep can step straight over a boundary and make an unstable chart look rock solid. Then we narrowed by bisection until the crossing was pinned to the second.

Result: the Moon leaves Chitra at 08:47:51 a.m. (using UTC+5:30, the offset almost every site assumes). Using UTC+6:30 — Indian War Time, which India actually observed from September 1942 to October 1945, and which was in force on his birth day — the same instant reads as 09:47:51 a.m.

Across the full day the Moon is in Chitra for about 39% of the hours and Swati for about 61%. Neither is a majority worth betting a whole page on.
LESSON 07

What we genuinely can't tell you

A chart has two halves. Which sign each planet is in — that needs only the date, and it is why this page exists. And the houses, including the rising sign or lagna, which need the exact minute of birth.

His birth time is rated DD on Astro-Databank — conflicting sources, nothing verified. The two circulating versions are twelve and a half hours apart, which moves the ascendant across most of the zodiac.

So on this page you will not see us say "his tenth house of career" or "Saturn in his eighth". That would be a guess wearing a lab coat. Plenty of sites will. The useful question to ask any of them is simply: which birth time did you use, and where did you get it?
LESSON 08

So — is Amitabh Bachchan manglik?

A frequently searched question, and the honest answer is unsatisfying.

"Manglik" (mangal dosha) depends on which house Mars occupies — the 1st, 2nd, 4th, 7th, 8th or 12th, depending on which tradition you follow. Houses need the birth minute. His is disputed by half a day.

What we can say, and it holds at every hour: his Mars sits in Virgo, a neutral sign for Mars, in Hasta nakshatra, and it is deeply combust — 1°36′ from the Sun. Whether it lands in a manglik house cannot be answered from anything public. Any site giving you a confident yes or no for him has silently chosen one of the two birth times.
LESSON 09

How to actually read that chart square

The grid earlier on this page is a South-Indian chart, the easiest of the three regional styles to learn, because the signs never move.

Twelve boxes around the edge, one per zodiac sign, always in the same places. Pisces top-left, then clockwise across the top, down the right side, back along the bottom, and up the left. Learn the ring once and you can read any South-Indian chart for the rest of your life.

Try it: find the box marked VIR. Four symbols sit in it — ☉ ☿ ♀ ♂. That is his Virgo stellium. You just read a kundli.
LESSON 10

Retrograde, without the drama

A word thrown around a lot that sounds far worse than it is.

Retrograde means a planet appeared to move backwards across the sky. It isn't actually reversing — it's an optical effect of Earth overtaking it in orbit, the way a slower car seems to slide backwards as you pass it. Traditionally it makes a planet's themes more internal and slower to show results.

His: Mercury and Saturn retrograde, plus Rahu and Ketu — and the nodes are retrograde essentially always by the standard calculation, so that pair is not a special flag on him.

Not a disaster either way. Anyone selling you a "remedy" for a retrograde node is selling you something.
LESSON 11

What this can and can't tell you

Worth being blunt, since this page has spent a while treating a horoscope as a serious object.

  • It can describe tendencies, and — given a verified minute — it can time long stretches. That part is arithmetic; two astrologers with the same birth data compute the same periods.
  • It can't tell you what someone does with those tendencies. A great many people share an exalted Mercury without becoming the most recognisable voice in a country of a billion.
  • It definitely can't explain, predict or excuse a real event — an accident, a company failing, a film landing. Anyone offering that certainty is guessing confidently.
The honest framing: a chart describes raw material and weather. It is not a script, it is not a verdict, and nothing on this page should be read as either.

Quick answers

What people ask about his kundli

FAQ 01

What is Amitabh Bachchan's birth time?

There isn't one agreed answer. Two versions circulate for 11 October 1942: 3:30 a.m. — he has himself said he was born between 3 and 4 in the morning — and 4:00 p.m., which matches his father's autobiography describing an early-afternoon birth and is what several astrology databases use. Astro-Databank rates his data DD, meaning conflicting and unverified. Because the two are twelve and a half hours apart, this page publishes only what the date settles — planet signs, dignities and nakshatra options — and never a rising sign or a house.

FAQ 02

What is Amitabh Bachchan's zodiac sign and nakshatra?

His Moon sits in Libra (Tula) — the rashi most Vedic answers actually mean — and it does so at every minute of his birth day, so that one is settled. His Sun is in Virgo (Kanya), which is what a Western-style answer would give. His birth nakshatra is not settled: the Moon leaves Chitra and enters Swati at 08:47 that morning, so the 3:30 a.m. version gives Chitra and the 4:00 p.m. version gives Swati. Both are printed confidently across the internet. Only one of them can be right, and nobody currently knows which.

FAQ 03

What is Amitabh Bachchan's mahadasha right now?

We can't tell you, and neither can anyone else honestly. The Vimshottari dasha sequence is generated entirely from the birth nakshatra — and his falls on a boundary that his two candidate birth times straddle. Chitra hands the sequence to Mars; Swati hands it to Rahu. That produces two different ladders of planets running for different lengths in a different order, so there is no single "current mahadasha" to state. Our full analysis of the dasha question is in Lesson 05 above. If you want a real dasha timeline, it needs a verified minute — ours computes yours from your own birth details in a few seconds.

FAQ 04

Is Amitabh Bachchan manglik?

Not answerable without a verified birth time. Manglik status depends on which house Mars occupies, and houses need the exact minute. What is certain at every hour of 11 October 1942: his Mars is in Virgo — a neutral sign for Mars — in Hasta nakshatra, and it is deeply combust, sitting 1°36′ from the Sun. Anyone giving you a firm yes or no has quietly chosen one of the two disputed times. See Lesson 08 for the long version.

Method. Every placement, degree, combustion figure and nakshatra boundary on this page is computed with the Swiss Ephemeris using the Lahiri ayanamsa — the same engine behind every AxtroShastra report — for 11 October 1942, Allahabad (25.44°N, 81.85°E). Because his birth time is disputed by more than twelve hours (Astro-Databank rating DD), we ran the chart at ten-minute intervals across the whole day and bisected to the second. All nine planet signs, all dignities, all combustion states and all retrogrades are identical at every hour, so those are published. The Moon's nakshatra is not: it crosses Chitra→Swati at 08:47:51 IST (09:47:51 under the Indian War Time UTC+6:30 offset actually in force in October 1942). Because the birth nakshatra alone generates the Vimshottari dasha sequence, no dasha order, no dated period and no current mahadasha appears anywhere on this page, and neither does any house, ascendant or manglik verdict.
